items.title: Democratization of capital market crucial for wealth generation
items.summary: Maputo, 15 Oct (AIM) – Mozambican President Daniel Chapo believes that greater democratization of the capital market is crucial for expansion of citizens’ access to business ownership and wealth generation within the country. Speaking on Wednesday, in Maputo, at the ceremony marking the 28th anniversary of the Mozambique Stock Exchange (BVM), compliance with legislation is crucial to attract more investors. The event also marked the listing of MECTS, S.A. (Mozambique Electronic Cargo Tracking Services, S.A.) as the first company governed by the legal framework for Public-Private Partnerships (PPPs). According to Chapo, opening the stock market to a broader range of Mozambican investors is essential for transforming citizens into direct participants in the ownership of productive assets, moving beyond their traditional roles as mere workers and consumers. The President also believes that the listing of MECTS should signal the beginning of a new phase in implementing legal mechanisms for national participation as 15 years have passed since the legal framework was approved.

items.title: Mozambique: Government authorises public auction of seized minerals during CAVAME-d conference in Nacala
items.summary: The decision was taken at the Council of Ministers’ 29th ordinary session on 13 October The seized minerals will be auctioned as part of the Conference on Adding Value to Mineral and Energy Resources – Available (CAVAME-d) and the Nacala Gem Fair (FAGENA). Both events will take place in the city of Nacala, Nampula Province, from 19 to 24 October 2026 The auction lots will include gemstones, precious and semi-precious stones and gold confiscated by the inspection authorities The minerals to be sold include rubies, tourmalines, aquamarines, garnets, topazes, tantalite and gold The initiative aims to strengthen transparency in the extractive sector and ensure that revenue from the sale of seized minerals goes directly to the state coffers The event also seeks to attract domestic and international buyers and investors to promote the local processing and transformation of minerals READ: Mozambique seeks investors for mineral value addition and processing as Nacala hosts CAVAME-d conference

items.title: Chapo calls for strengthened measures against drug trafficking
items.summary: Maputo, 15 Oct (AIM) – Mozambican President Daniel Chapo has pledged to intensify the fight against drug trafficking and consumption, with particular focus on protecting schools from drug networks targeting children and adolescents. Speaking on Wednesday in Maputo, at the opening of the National Conference on Drug Prevention and Control, held under the motto “Drug prevention and control: new trends, challenges and innovative responses”, Chapo challenged the Attorney General’s Office (PGR), the courts, the Defence and Security Forces and the National Criminal Investigation Service (SERNIC) to identify and dismantle drug-selling and consumption points, commonly known as “drug dens”. He said those involved must be held accountable and subjected to the criminal penalties provided for by law. “But it is the school that is now my deepest concern. Schools should be temples of knowledge and safe havens for our sons and daughters, but they are being targeted by drug networks”, he said.

items.title: School roof collapse in Pakistan's Peshawar kills at least 17 students
items.summary: Local authorities said more than three dozen other people were injured in the disaster. Roof collapses have become increasingly common in Pakistan Officials in Peshawar, Pakistan, confirmed on Thursday that at least 27 pupils under the age of 13 died when a school roof collapsed in the Afridi Abad area of the city One teacher has also died, they said. The deceased, along with more than 40 other injured people, were brought to Lady Reading Hospital as rescue workers rushed to clear the rubble and search for more survivors The cause of the disaster was not immediately clear Local media in Pakistan noted that such incidents are becoming increasingly routine across the country, due to poor building standards and maintenance In July, three young girls were killed near Umerkot when the outer wall of a government school gave way.

items.title: Zimbabwean author denies using AI to write award-winning story
items.summary: Simbarashe Kundizeza says he was inspired by a poem about fish tanks to write a story about his family struggles in Zimbabwe Zimbabwean writer Simbarashe Kundizeza has denied using artificial intelligence (AI) to write his short story, which won this year's Caine Prize for African Writing His statement comes a week after he scooped the £10,000 ($13,000) award and a recent article in The Atlantic said AI-detection software Pangram had shown his work about a boy whose family falls on hard times was entirely AI generated "For the avoidance of doubt, I wrote The Blue Fighter," he posted on X , external The accusation has caused an uproar on social media and Caine Prize chair Ellah Wakatama told the BBC she was shocked that the US magazine had not waited for a full investigation before publishing "I do wish The Atlantic had spent more time investigating this so that alongside Pangram, they did have evidence of real human investigation of it before tainting the prize and tainting this winner," Wakatama told the BBC's Front Row programme The chair of the Caine Prize's board of trustees…

items.title: Climate change and drone attacks exacerbate the humanitarian crisis in war-torn Sudan
items.summary: Aid groups warn of an imminent collapse of the health system as fighting continues to displace civilians amid the planting season. The UN has extended an arms embargo, but only for Darfur In Sudan , clashes between the Sudanese Armed Forces (SAF) and the Rapid Support Forces (RSF) have intensified in North Kordofan and parts of Blue Nile state. The fighting has forced thousands of civilians to flee amid the planting season Since war broke out between the two factions and their allied militias in April 2023, both sides have fought for power . However, neither has managed to establish control over the entire country The SAF, the nation's official army, is in control of Sudan's north and center, including the capital, Khartoum, while the RSF maintains its presence in the western Darfur region and parts of the south The brutal war has plunged Sudan into one of the world's worst humanitarian and displacement crises, according to the United Nations and international aid organizations.
